lessons.title: Waking up and getting ready
lessons.tip:
The present tense is the infinitive + -r, the same for every person: ringe becomes ringer, vågne becomes vågner, barbere becomes barberer. Short stems like stå and tage give står and tager.
Example: Hun står op. (She gets up.)

lessons.title: Reflexive pronouns and "in the morning"
lessons.tip:
With reflexive verbs the pronoun matches the subject: jeg ... mig, du ... dig, han/hun/de ... sig, vi ... os, I ... jer.
To say when something usually happens, use om + part of day or weekday + -en: om morgenen, om mandagen. Weekend is different: i weekenden.

lessons.title: Where "always" and "never" go
lessons.tip:
Central adverbs (altid, normalt, tit, nogle gange, aldrig, ikke, kun) come after the verb: S - V - CA. In a yes/no question the verb comes first: V - S - CA.
A reflexive pronoun comes before the adverb (Jeg barberer mig altid); a particle like op comes after it (Jeg står altid op).

lessons.title: Everyday activities (1)
lessons.tip:
The present tense is the infinitive + -r (most verbs ending in -e just add -r), and it is the same for every person: jeg, du, han, hun, vi, I, de all use the same form. Gøre is irregular: gør.
Example: Hun køber ind. (She does the shopping.)

lessons.title: Starting a sentence with the time
lessons.tip:
Many time and place expressions (and most central adverbs) can start a sentence. The verb still comes second, so the subject moves after it: S - V becomes A - V - S. Først, så and bagefter work the same way.
Example: Om morgenen er Thomas tit træt. (In the morning Thomas is often tired.)

lessons.title: The Dam family: a busy home
lessons.tip:
When one subject has several verbs, join them with og and do not repeat the subject: S - V - og - V. With inversion: A - V - S - og - V.
Example: Hun køber ind og laver mad. (She does the shopping and cooks.)

lessons.title: Recap: the Dam family and Bente
lessons.tip:
Word order with central adverbs and several verbs: S - V - CA, with inversion A - V - S - CA. With one subject and several verbs: S - V - CA - og - V.
Example: Om morgenen drikker hun altid te og spiser brød.
context: Jens and Eva Dam are married with three children and share the housework.
Eva always does the shopping on the way home from work. Eva does the laundry and Jens washes the car.
Jens is a morning person and is often tired in the evening.
The family often has guests at the weekend. Eva is sometimes cross, and they argue.
Bente is a morning person: she is always fresh in the morning and often wakes up at five.
She normally takes a shower and washes her hair, then always reads the paper. She also listens to the radio.
She doesn't eat breakfast very often. She only drinks a cup of coffee and is never hungry in the morning.
She normally goes to work at quarter to six. After work she sometimes visits a friend.
She always eats dinner at six. In the evening she normally listens to music and drinks tea.
She always goes to bed at ten and is often tired in the evening.

lessons.title: Recap: Nick's week
context: Nick lives with his girlfriend Anna in Odense. They have no children.
He wakes up at 7. First he eats breakfast, then he brushes his teeth, afterwards he has a shower and shaves.
For breakfast he has bread, cheese and coffee, no tea.
He works at Nokia from 8:00 to 16:00, 20 minutes away by car.
In the evening he eats dinner at 18:30, afterwards relaxes or plays computer games, and goes to bed at 24:00.
At home Nick cooks and Anna does the dishes. They clean and shop together.
On Saturday morning he first reads the paper, then shops, afterwards eats lunch. On Sunday they have guests, go for a walk and visit friends.
